evals.name: trace-utility-copy-edits
evals.prompt: dx-review #745. Dry run: don't post or push. Review it as of commit 98504993e0 (the author's last commit before reviewer edits).
evals.expected_output: Ground truth: the docs lead pushed two 'copy edits' commits (8cead9bd6a, 849e27096b): sentence-case titles ('Diagnose preview rebuilds', 'TurboSnap dependency tracing'), bold numbered items turned into '### 1. Imperative' headings, gerund headings to imperatives, 'you'll need to' cut, em dashes removed, 'ex.' → 'such as', heading levels fixed, decorative bold removed. Verdict: approve with thanks.
assertions: Converts title-case titles/H1s to sentence case (e.g. 'Diagnosing Preview Rebuilds' / 'TurboSnap Dependency Tracing')
Turns bold numbered list items into real '### N. Imperative' step headings
Removes em dashes from prose sentences in changed lines
Replaces 'ex.' with 'e.g.' or 'such as'
Raises overlap/placement with existing TurboSnap docs as a question rather than moving content across pages
Verdict is APPROVE
Review body reads like a short colleague note: under ~60 words, no markdown headings or bullet summary
Copy edits are delivered as a patch (copy-edits.patch is non-empty) rather than only as comments asking the author to reword

evals.name: mock-debugging-accuracy
evals.prompt: can you take a pass at chromatic-docs PR 661? just draft it, don't post anything. Review the state at commit 6be12047e9.
evals.expected_output: Ground truth: the docs lead challenged the claim that the Storybook Test addon / Test Runner / a 'Test Hook API' affect how Chromatic waits for mocked data ('Chromatic doesn't use either of those tools'; no API to wait for mocked data), pointed to the assertion approach instead. Copy edits: FAQ summary as a full question ('Why are stories with mocked data…'), 'expression' → 'assertion', interaction test step before delays. Verdict should not approve the inaccurate claim as-is.
assertions: Questions the claim that the Storybook Test addon / Test Runner / a test hook affects how Chromatic waits for mocked data
Does not silently rewrite that technical claim in the patch (asks instead)
Verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT, not a plain APPROVE
FAQ <summary>/heading phrased as a full natural question
Review body reads like a short colleague note: under ~60 words, no markdown headings or bullet summary
Copy edits are delivered as a patch (copy-edits.patch is non-empty) rather than only as comments asking the author to reword

evals.name: snapshot-instability-questions
evals.prompt: Review deandre's PR #923 (snapshot instability causes) as of commit fa9f953ac6 — dry run only, I'll post it myself.
evals.expected_output: Ground truth: the docs lead left question comments, no commits: 'If it is, then what should the user do?' (missing next step), 'can we show an example?', 'Could you explain here what a "fractional element" means. Maybe even put that in the title', and noted an example is inside an accordion above so repeat or link it. Verdict: comment/request changes with questions, plus any pure copy edits.
assertions: Asks what the reader should do next where a cause is described without a fix
Asks for a definition of 'fractional element' (or suggests putting it in the heading)
Asks for an example, or to repeat/link an example that is hidden in an accordion
Verdict is COMMENT or REQUEST_CHANGES (questions block)
Inline comments are short (most under ~40 words) and conversational
Review body reads like a short colleague note: under ~60 words, no markdown headings or bullet summary
Copy edits are delivered as a patch (copy-edits.patch is non-empty) rather than only as comments asking the author to reword

evals.name: faq-chromatic-entity
evals.prompt: dx-review https://github.com/chromaui/chromatic-docs/pull/676 — dry run against commit b8f831be6a please
evals.expected_output: Ground truth: the docs lead asked 'what is a "Chromatic entity"?' and pushed copy edits (578507d90f): cut the 'There's no automation (yet!)…Here's how' lead-in to 'To migrate your Chromatic projects to the new Git provider:', Oxford comma ('steps 1, 3, and 4'), 'Chromatic entity' → organization account wording, 'Profile' → 'Profile page'. Comment: 'made some copy edits, does this work for you?'
assertions: Questions or replaces the undefined term 'Chromatic entity'
Cuts the 'There's no automation (yet!)… Here's how' lead-in down to a direct instruction
Adds the Oxford comma in 'steps 1, 3, and 4'
Review body mentions the pushed copy edits and invites the author to check them (e.g. 'LMK if they look okay')
Review body reads like a short colleague note: under ~60 words, no markdown headings or bullet summary
Copy edits are delivered as a patch (copy-edits.patch is non-empty) rather than only as comments asking the author to reword
